newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Farmer sales stall again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Farmer sales stall again.

text.p: Spring wheat farmers once again held tightly to new crop supplies after briefly loosening their grip on Friday, several cash grain dealers said.
"The board continues to go down, the basis kind of slipped and the farmer is a bit upset," a Minnesota dealer said. "He's just going to sit tight for a while."
Bids were steady to lower, in line with a 3/4 cent per bushel drop in MGE December spring wheat futures.
MGE December wheat closed at $3.84-1/4 cents per bushel on Monday, a fresh contract low. Prices had peaked at $6.34 in May.
Selling had picked up slightly on Friday as farmers began to lose hope of a rebound in prices, merchants said.
But dealers noted that farmers sold only enough to pay end-of-the-month bills. Many continued to hold onto ideas that prices would recover after the sharp drop this fall.
But dealers also noted competing countries were harvesting bumper crops and U.S. wheat was overvalued compared to prices in Argentina.
